title: Set a static IP address with netplan

ADDRESS.means: the new address with its prefix, e.g. 192.0.2.20/24

steps.say: Other netplan files: if one also sets this interface, the settings merge.
Back up the current netplan files.
Create a new file with this content (spaces only, no tabs).
steps.rollback: Delete the file, then run sudo netplan apply.
steps.content:
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    <IFACE>:
      dhcp4: false
      addresses: [<ADDRESS>]
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: <GATEWAY>
      nameservers:
        addresses: [<DNS>]

steps.say: Only root may read it (netplan warns about open permissions).
Check the files for mistakes without applying them.
steps.rollback: Nothing applied yet: delete the file to undo.

steps.say: Apply with automatic rollback: press Enter within 120 seconds to keep it.
steps.rollback: If the connection drops, do nothing: it reverts by itself after 120 seconds.

steps.say: The default route uses the new gateway.

pitfalls: On a remote server, never use netplan apply for this: a mistake cuts you off. Use netplan try.
If cloud-init manages the network, it may rewrite /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml. Check that file's header.
